title: Zanzibar Revolution
summary: On 12 January 1964 armed insurgents on Unguja, the main island of Zanzibar, overthrew the Sultan, Jamshid bin Abdullah, and his mainly Arab government. Violence against Arab and South Asian civilians followed; the death toll is disputed. Abeid Karume became president, and in April a union with Tanganyika to form Tanzania was announced.

uncertainty.note: Outbreak 12 January 1964; the aftermath ran on for months.

where.modern_name: Stone Town, Zanzibar, Tanzania (proxy pin for Zanzibar Town on Unguja)

importance.justification: Ended Arab-led rule of Zanzibar and led to the union that created Tanzania.

audience_note: Includes massacres, rapes and looting directed at Arab and South Asian civilians; death toll estimates range from hundreds to 20,000.

sources.title: The Racialization of Politics in Revolutionary Zanzibar (honors thesis)
sources.publisher: United States Naval Academy, History Department
sources.author: Hettiger

reviewer_note: Pin is a proxy: UNESCO's Stone Town centre point converted from degrees-minutes-seconds. Summary details beyond the date (Karume, April union, disputed toll) rest on the Wikipedia FA only. Death toll deliberately not given as a single figure.
